title: Aaron Burr to Theodosia Burr Alston, Baltimore, 31 January, 10 and 18 February [1808]: period-6 Vigenere sheets filed with GLC01523

documents.shelfmark: Gilder Lehrman Collection, GLC01523 (sheet pencilled 1523A, sections B and C)
documents.date: 31 Jan [1808] (copy sent with the 10 Feb letter)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the sheets; Gilder Lehrman calls them undecoded; nothing in Davis 1837 or in Kline 1983's table of contents.

documents.shelfmark: Gilder Lehrman Collection, GLC01523 (sheet pencilled 1523A, section A)

transcription.notes: Superscript figures with a caret are insertions; three without a caret (A.06, A.07) are not part of the cipher.

documents.shelfmark: Gilder Lehrman Collection, GLC01523 (sheet docketed 'Balt.' and '1808')

transcription.notes: One four-number group rubbed on a fold (2?,11?,1,23); one group struck through by Burr and rewritten.

system.summary: Vigenere over the alphabet numbered a=1 ... z=26, period 6 (shifts 6 18 22 7 24 8), key running through the letters and restarting at each section; words divided.
system.notes: Numbers of a word joined by commas or dots, words by spaces. No keyword behind the shifts found (a=0 GSWHYI). The July 1804 letter on the same file uses a simple substitution (burr1804).

prior_solution.where: Gilder Lehrman (catalogue, AMDigital, Hamilton Education Program) treats the sheets as the 1804 letter's pages and says undecoded; Davis 1837 has no letters Oct 1807 - June 1808; Kline 1983's table of contents has no Jan-Feb 1808 letter (the vol. 2 editorial note 'The Road to Exile' was not read); not on cryptiana or DECODE.

conditions.human_role: Project owner pasted the catalogue 2049 contributor task; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Hamilton Education Program page: page PNGs of GLC01523.
Section A of img1 transcribed (80 words, 341 numbers 1-26).
Flat frequencies, all 26 values; one 6-number word three times running; IoC 0.0435 overall, 0.0618 at period 6.
Monoalphabetic ruled out (doubled numbers that cannot be double letters, impossible two-letter words).
Column chi-square against English letter frequencies at periods 3, 6, 12; period 6 gives shifts 6 18 22 7 24 8 and section A reads; period 3 fails.
Sections B, C of img1 and img2 transcribed; caretless superscripts left out after they broke the decode.
resync.py: Viterbi over words scored with the en-modern model finds two key-phase slips: Burr's omitted s in 'best', and a rubbed group in img2.
Davis's text of Burr's 18 July 1804 letter, 341 letters, enciphered with 20 random 6-place keys; the same solver recovers the key 20/20.
Every section reads with the same key; torn edge numbers completed from the key; 973 numbers, 969 give sense.
Docket 'Balt.' '1808' and content (Baltimore incog., long voyage, The Oaks, 'mari') date the sheets to Jan-Feb 1808 and make Theodosia the recipient, not part of the July 1804 letter.
Davis 1837 (Gutenberg) grepped; Kline 1983 table of contents via archive.org search-inside; cryptiana; DECODE harvest: no prior reading.
Keyword behind the shifts: all 26 alphabet offsets and the reversed form tried; none spells a word.
Rubbed img2 group tried at all six key places with 3 and 4 numbers: no word fits before 'hourly'.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 969 tokens, 136 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.211 per letter; random keys -7.468 (z 21.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.054 (mean -4.182, z 25.6); annealer on the real text -3.573. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.211; polyphony 0.0; 4 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.573

outcome.method_basis: The period and the six shifts were found by the index of coincidence and column frequency fitting on the cipher alone; nothing on the sheets or in print gave plaintext or a key.

texts.label: Copy of the letter of 31 January [1808] (img1, sections B and C)
texts.summary: Burr, hiding at Baltimore, tells Theodosia he still holds to his plans, is distressed that waiting to see him keeps her at The Oaks at risk to her health, and will try to reach her or send an express; no one is to know he means to visit South Carolina, and all but her husband are to think he is in Philadelphia.

reading_review.note: Reads as sentences; 'be[s]t' Burr's omission, two torn numbers completed from the key.

texts.label: Baltimore, 10 February [1808] (img1, section A)
texts.summary: A cover note sending the copy of 31 January by the schooner Wolf: still at Baltimore incognito, business detains him ten days more, the promise in his last letter was rashly made, affairs begin to look up.

reading_review.note: Reads as sentences; 'in' read against one number (15,16 gives 'ix').

texts.label: Baltimore, 18 February [1808] (img2)
texts.summary: Nothing new: the same hopes and intentions; he waits hourly for money for 'the long voyage' (he sailed for England in June 1808), and nothing else keeps him.

reading_review.note: Reads as sentences with one rubbed group open; 'have' and 'detains' each read against one number.

outcome.notes: Filed with the July 1804 letter GLC01523 as its 'pp. 2-3 in cipher' (catalogue 2049); a different cipher and date.
